passage: Harsha, you asked why I'm up till midnight, so here it is. I'm Uday. I found this speaker online in the summer, and his videos make life feel clear. He talks about waking early, being kind, having a purpose, and for the first time I feel like someone explains why I get up. I've watched every video, some twice. Last week you sent me a talk by a different speaker on the same idea, and they disagreed on one point. That bothered me at first, then I liked it. Now I keep a note of what each video asks me to do: wake early, help at home, nothing about money. I still like him. I just compare now.

qa.q: When did Uday find the speaker online?
qa.a: Uday found the speaker in the summer.

qa.q: What is Uday feeling about the speaker, and what shows it?
qa.a: Uday admires the speaker; watching every video, some twice, and feeling that life is clear show it. 🙂

qa.q: What is the benefit of Uday's habit of noting what each video asks?
qa.a: It lets Uday compare speakers and see what is being asked, such as habits and not money, so enjoying the videos does not turn into blind following.

qa.q: How might Harsha see Uday's late nights and the different talk Harsha sent?
qa.a: Harsha probably cares and wanted Uday to hear another view, and Uday's reaction shows Harsha's suggestion was welcome.

grounding: Uday admires an online speaker who makes life feel clear, and enjoys the videos while comparing sources and noting what they ask.
